it-2008-it-45.approach: Prim grows ONE connected tree: every new edge must touch the current tree and be the cheapest edge leaving it. First discard sequences whose edges are not connected to the tree built so far, then replay the survivor with weights.

Add $a$: $a$-$b=1$ is cheapest → $(a,b)$. Leaving edges now: $c$-$e=7$, $f$-$h=8$, $d$-$g=10$ → $(c,e)$.
Then $f$-$h=8$ beats $e$-$h=12$, $d$-$g=10$ → $(f,h)$. From $h$: $h$-$g=7$ → $(g,h)$; then $g$-$i=3$ → $(g,i)$.
Every choice is the minimum crossing edge, so (C) is a valid Prim execution. Total weight $2+3+5+1+7+8+7+3=36$.

steps.body: Sequence is always produce, consume, produce, consume, … — every value is consumed before the next is produced (no loss), each thread always gets its turn (no starvation), and one semaphore is always available to some thread (no deadlock).

it-2008-it-65.verification: Units: $\mu s\times$ Gbps $=10^{-6}\times10^9 = 10^3$ bits per µs; 2 µs → 2000 bits.

it-2008-it-66.approach: Recompute every row and column parity of the received 5×8 block. Each corrupted bit flips exactly one row check and one column check, so the minimum number of errors is at least the number of failing columns (and rows); then show that many flips suffice.

steps.title: Lower bound
steps.body: A single flipped bit changes the parity of exactly one column. Three columns fail, so at least **3** bits are corrupted.

steps.title: Three flips suffice
steps.body: Flip $(r_1,d_5)$, $(r_4,d_2)$, $(r_4,d_0)$: column $d_5$, $d_2$, $d_0$ each toggled once ✓; row $r_1$ toggled once ✓; row $r_4$ toggled twice (stays even) ✓. All checks pass, so $n_{min}=3$.

scene.caption: Flipping these 3 bits makes every parity even

optionAnalysis.reason: One error flips one row and one column, but three columns fail.
Two flips can fix at most two failing columns; three fail.
Three failing columns force ≥ 3 errors, and the three flips shown fix every check.
Not minimal — 3 flips already make the block consistent.

pitfalls: Forgetting to check the parity column d0 and parity row r4 themselves.
Counting failing rows plus columns as the number of errors.
it-2008-it-66.verification: After the three flips: r1 = 1110111|0 (6 ones), r4 = 1100001|1 (4 ones), every column sum even.
